records.finding: Refined the Jiahu event with the full paper assigning the inference to Period III. The comparative fish-size method and sample proportions support possible management, with no dated structure or transfer from Jiahu to a later community. The modern rice-field comparison supplies a test case, and Jiahu rice use gives no evidence of integrated rice–fish farming.

sources.locator: Nakajima et al. (2019), pp. 1415–1417, Fig. 1b–d and 1i and Methods
sources.note: Uses excavated teeth and a modern comparative sample. The modern sample does not date ancient field or pond use.

Examines historical sources independently of the archaeological work. The earliest transmitted text attributed to Fan Li is preserved in the sixth-century Qimin yaoshu; a c. 500 BCE text date is unwarranted.

records.next: Compare excavation plans and faunal distributions for Period III with independent early finds or texts between Jiahu and later managed ponds.

records.finding: Added a dated macrobotanical witness for one Donghulin deposit with charred grains identified as foxtail millet. Starch and charred grain studies partly share personnel and excavations but examine different material. This supports early millet use without demonstrating how it led to later farming.

sources.locator: Zhao et al. (2020), Tables 2–4, pp. 103–104, sample BA07888
sources.note: A date on a seed from one millet-bearing deposit, not on the millet. Authors discuss possible displacement of small charred grains.

sources.locator: Yang et al. (2012), Results and Discussion
sources.note: Studies ground-stone and pottery starch residues; some wild and domesticated reference material overlaps.
Reports directly dated charred millets identified morphologically at Xinglonggou, a later northeastern site with no measured continuity from Donghulin.

records.next: Seek direct dates on the Donghulin grains and systematically screened intervening assemblages between the earliest grinding residues and larger village crop assemblages.

records.finding: Proposed a site-specific wetland cultivation record and a companion link asking whether cultivated rice or its processing remnants were used to feed managed pigs at Kuahuqiao. Pig calculus documents exposure to rice and prepared foods. Field source and deliberate feeding remain unresolved, and the candidate applies only to Kuahuqiao.

sources.note: Original dental calculus and metric evidence. Authors relate site differences to subsistence and environment. Rice residue identifies consumption, not field source or feeding arrangement.

sources.locator: Zheng et al. (2007), pp. 1655–1657 and Table 1
sources.note: Rice grains and husk remains complement sediment and dental samples, with overlap of some researchers between this study and the later pig study.
Separate observations contest which vegetation was burned. The abstract was the accessible part.

records.next: Seek feeding contexts and phase-matched evidence linking a dated managed pig assemblage to rice or residues of rice processing from local cultivated plants.

records.finding: Added a research question supported by directly inspected tool-use evidence. Stone-flake panicle harvesting at Shangshan is supported by separate use-wear and residue observations, but neither the different rice morphology samples nor the harvesting study ties it to emergence of the particular phytolith traits. Subsequent shifts towards stalk harvesting are evidence from later contexts, especially Hehuashan.

sources.note: SS-10 is a Shangshan specimen. The selective effect depends on seed retention for sowing and is inferred; the tool evidence focuses on technique.
Original rachilla observations on distinct rice material, independent of the use-wear result.

sources.locator: Zuo et al. (2017), Abstract and Discussion
sources.note: Earlier record studies phytolith morphology; the marker differs from non-shattering, the trait discussed in the harvesting model.

records.next: Look for phase-matched harvesting tools and quantified, independently dated seed or spikelet populations with evidence of retained sowing stock.

records.next: Seek a series of dated seed measurements and farming-context evidence spanning the earlier local pottery impressions, Middle Jomon assemblage and later soybean cultivation.

records.finding: Added local context and an attributed explanation of engineered water management at Caoxieshan. Earlier Kuahuqiao wetland cultivation is a documented comparator, but its particular field engineering and transmission into the Lake Tai region are unproved. Tianluoshan’s excavated early horizons lack the comparable ditch-and-bund layout. At Maoshan and later Shiao, larger layouts document later regional practice. The existing Liangzhu city and Song-era Champa rice records add a regional urban and a much later seed-transmission comparison, respectively. None identifies the builders or users of these Late Majiabang fields as their source.

records.next: Cross-match the Lake Tai field contexts against original plans and calibrated phases. Seek a shared local sequence showing how and where the small ditch-linked plots changed into later designs.
